items.comparator: Previous process: around eight design–make–test cycles, with each cycle taking eight weeks.
items.quantitative_outcome: Reuters reported: AI cut the number of design, manufacture and test cycles “from around eight to three” and “slashed the time of each cycle from eight weeks to four.”
items.signal: A reported reduction in both iteration count and cycle duration suggests a workflow-throughput benefit in molecule development. It is a weak signal of competitive advantage: the report does not provide an independent evaluation or a like-for-like non-AI control.
items.source: Reuters report carried by The Sacramento Bee

items.signal: Merck is supplying selected proprietary research datasets for use with Isomorphic Labs’ AI drug-design engine in a collaboration focused on an undisclosed oncology target. This is a distinctive data-access move that could support an advantage, but the report gives no outcome, dataset details, or evidence of exclusivity.

items.comparator: Query times improved from roughly 20–30 seconds to about 2–3 seconds; Microsoft describes this as around 90%.
items.quantitative_outcome: Microsoft reports: “Financial crime query time cut by 90%.” The accompanying detail says query times improved from roughly 20–30 seconds to about 2–3 seconds.
items.signal: AI-enabled financial-crime query workflow with a reported reduction in query time. The source does not state a broader competitive advantage or a head-to-head competitor comparison.
items.source: Microsoft Cloud Blog; Microsoft reported the case-study outcome.

items.comparator: Compared with the researchers’ approximately nine-month analysis of the same vulnerability-research task; the source does not specify a separate non-AI control protocol.
items.quantitative_outcome: “The AI-assisted approach reduced analysis time from approximately nine months to 90 hours and uncovered 99 vulnerabilities, including 66 that were previously unknown.” The company also reported automated static analysis cost of $935 total, averaging $2.58 per finding.
items.signal: A reported large reduction in vulnerability-analysis time alongside discovery of previously unknown flaws. The work used off-the-shelf AI and covered 10 TCP/IP stacks, so the result suggests an efficiency signal but does not establish that the advantage is hard for competitors to copy.
items.source: Forescout Technologies / Vedere Labs announcement, as reproduced by Yahoo Finance

items.comparator: No explicit baseline or named comparator stated; the source describes manual effort and throughput but provides no before/after throughput figure.
items.quantitative_outcome: The source states the AI-based Fabrication Planner demonstrated the ability to “reduce manual effort by up to 60% while maximizing throughput.” It also says P&ID compliance checks that take engineers hours now run in minutes, without giving exact times.
items.signal: Octave Intelligence reported results from its co-innovation program with MAIRE, which used customer engineering and operational data to build an AI-based fabrication planner and P&ID checks. Potentially distinctive access to MAIRE’s project data and workflows is suggested, but no details establish exclusivity.
items.source: Octave Intelligence company announcement, distributed by GlobeNewswire

items.comparator: The reported comparison is the router’s own power draw before and during the AI-optimized setting; the article does not give a separate baseline consumption figure. Service KPIs were reportedly unaffected.
items.quantitative_outcome: The article reports that power consumption fell by 5–6% on Salam’s IP network. It says the result was measured on one Huawei NE8000 X8 router over 39 hours, with power draw recorded every 15 minutes; no service degradation alarms were raised.
items.signal: A live-network trial is a measured operating result, but the report describes a joint Salam–Huawei proof of concept, not evidence that the result is difficult for competitors to reproduce.
items.source: MENAFN, reporting on Salam’s work with Huawei

items.comparator: AEP’s previous process for candidate-resource data updates in the production workbook behind its integrated resource plan; the report gives the old and new durations.
items.quantitative_outcome: The source states AEP cut candidate-resource data updates “from three weeks to three days.” It also reports that PLEXOS Intelligence handled 70% to 80% of the input work.
items.signal: Energy Exemplar says AEP used the tool on its production IRP workbook. The quantified workflow gain is notable, though the report does not establish that the underlying data or capability is exclusive to AEP.
items.source: Energy Exemplar announcement, distributed by EIN Presswire
